import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

lemma Consistent.of_le {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Consistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢) : Consistent 𝓣 :=
  ⟨fun H ↦ not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr (H.of_ge h) h𝓢⟩

namespace Logic

protected def Inconsistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Inconsistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma inconsistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Inconsistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

protected def Consistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Consistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma consistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Consistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Consistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[ext] structure Translation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  toFun : F → F'
  prf {f} : 𝓢 ⊢ f → 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f

infix:40 " ↝ " => Translation

@[ext] structure Bitranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  r : 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣
  l : 𝓣 ↝ 𝓢
  r_l : r.toFun ∘ l.toFun = id
  l_r : l.toFun ∘ r.toFun = id

infix:40 " ↭ " => Bitranslation

@[ext] structure FaithfulTranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') extends 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣 where
  prfInv {f} : 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f → 𝓢 ⊢ f

infix:40 " ↝¹ " => FaithfulTranslation
annotation: infix:40 " ↝¹ " => FaithfulTranslation

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

lemma Consistent.of_le {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Consistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢) : Consistent 𝓣 :=
  ⟨fun H ↦ not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr (H.of_ge h) h𝓢⟩

namespace Logic

protected def Inconsistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Inconsistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma inconsistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Inconsistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

protected def Consistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Consistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma consistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Consistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Consistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[ext] structure Translation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  toFun : F → F'
  prf {f} : 𝓢 ⊢ f → 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f

infix:40 " ↝ " => Translation

@[ext] structure Bitranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  r : 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣
  l : 𝓣 ↝ 𝓢
  r_l : r.toFun ∘ l.toFun = id
  l_r : l.toFun ∘ r.toFun = id

infix:40 " ↭ " => Bitranslation

@[ext] structure FaithfulTranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') extends 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣 where
  prfInv {f} : 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f → 𝓢 ⊢ f

infix:40 " ↝¹ " => FaithfulTranslation
annotation: infix:40 " ↝¹ " => FaithfulTranslation

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

<STATEMENT>

For any formulas $φ$ and $ψ$, and any set of formulas $\mathcal{S}$, the class `Deduction` specifies that adding $φ$ to $\mathcal{S}$ yields $ψ$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}$ alone proves that $φ$ implies $ψ$.

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

To understand the behavior of the `Deduction` class, we consider its two components, `ofInsert` and `inv`.

1. **Understanding `ofInsert`:** The `ofInsert` method tells us that if by adding $φ$ to the set $\mathcal{S}$ we can derive $ψ$ (i.e., `cons φ �� ⊢ ψ`), then we can conclude that within the original set $\mathcal{S}$ alone, $φ$ implies $ψ$ (i.e., `$\mathcal{S} ⊢ φ ➝ ψ$`). This axiom essentially says that adding a premise should not allow us to derive something that wasn't already provable without it.

2. **Understanding `inv`:** Conversely, the `inv` method indicates that if within the set $\mathcal{S}$ alone we can establish that $φ$ implies $ψ$ (i.e., `$\mathcal{S} ⊢ φ ➝ ψ$`), then by adding $φ$ to $\mathcal{S}$, we can derive $ψ$ (i.e., `cons φ �� ⊢ ψ`). This ensures that if a conditional relationship holds without an additional premise, adding that premise maintains the derivability of the consequent.

Together, these axioms provide foundational rules for how conclusions can be drawn within the deductive system defined by the `Deduction` class. They ensure a certain consistency and coherence in the way formulas are added and implications are derived within the system.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

variable {F : Type*} {S : Type*} {T : Type*} {U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]
informal_statement: A set \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent if and only if every finite filter contained within \( \mathcal{S} \) is also consistent.
informal_proof:
To prove the equivalence, we address both directions of the statement.

**Forward Direction**: 
Assume that \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent. We need to show that every finite filter \( \mathcal{F} \) contained within \( \mathcal{S} \) is also consistent. Given the definition of consistency, if \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent, any finite subset or substructure within \( \mathcal{S} \), such as a finite filter \( \mathcal{F} \), preserves the necessary properties that define consistency. Thus, \( \mathcal{F} \) must inherit the consistency from \( \mathcal{S} \).

**Reverse Direction**: 
Conversely, suppose that every finite filter \( \mathcal{F} \) contained within \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent. We aim to show that \( \mathcal{S} \) itself is consistent. If \( \mathcal{S} \) were inconsistent, there would exist at least one filter that violates the consistency condition. However, by our assumption, all such finite filters within \( \mathcal{S} \) are consistent, implying that \( \mathcal{S} \) cannot contain any inconsistencies, thereby establishing its own consistency.

Hence, \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent if and only if every finite filter within it is consistent.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

lemma Consistent.of_le {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Consistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢) : Consistent 𝓣 :=
  ⟨fun H ↦ not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr (H.of_ge h) h𝓢⟩

namespace Logic

protected def Inconsistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Inconsistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma inconsistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Inconsistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

protected def Consistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Consistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma consistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Consistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Consistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[ext] structure Translation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  toFun : F → F'
  prf {f} : 𝓢 ⊢ f → 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f

infix:40 " ↝ " => Translation

@[ext] structure Bitranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  r : 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣
  l : 𝓣 ↝ 𝓢
  r_l : r.toFun ∘ l.toFun = id
  l_r : l.toFun ∘ r.toFun = id

infix:40 " ↭ " => Bitranslation

@[ext] structure FaithfulTranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') extends 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣 where
  prfInv {f} : 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f → 𝓢 ⊢ f

informal_statement: A set of statements is inconsistent if and only if there exists a finite subset of the set that is also inconsistent.
informal_proof:
First, we consider the forward direction. Assume we have an inconsistent set of statements. By the compactness theorem, if a set of statements is inconsistent, then there exists a finite subset of that set which is also inconsistent. This is because inconsistency implies the existence of a finite contradiction, isolated from the rest of the infinite set.

For the reverse direction, assume there exists a finite subset of the set that is inconsistent. Since any subset of a consistent set is also consistent, it follows that the entire set must be inconsistent. This is because if the entire set were consistent, then its subset would also have to be consistent, which contradicts our assumption.

Thus, both directions have been proven, establishing that a set of statements is inconsistent if and only if there exists a finite subset of the set that is also inconsistent.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

lemma Consistent.of_le {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Consistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢) : Consistent 𝓣 :=
  ⟨fun H ↦ not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr (H.of_ge h) h𝓢⟩

namespace Logic

protected def Inconsistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Inconsistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma inconsistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Inconsistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

protected def Consistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Consistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma consistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Consistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Consistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[ext] structure Translation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  toFun : F → F'
  prf {f} : 𝓢 ⊢ f → 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f

@[ext] structure Bitranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  r : 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣
  l : 𝓣 ↝ 𝓢
  r_l : r.toFun ∘ l.toFun = id
  l_r : l.toFun ∘ r.toFun = id

infix:40 " ↭ " => Bitranslation

@[ext] structure FaithfulTranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') extends 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣 where
  prfInv {f} : 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f → 𝓢 ⊢ f

informal_statement: A logical system is consistent if and only if it does not prove the contradiction symbol `⊥`. In other words, a system is consistent exactly when it is impossible to derive both a statement and its negation; equivalently, a system is consistent if it cannot prove a contradiction.
informal_proof:
To establish the equivalence, we will consider both directions of the biconditional statement.

**Forward Direction (Consistency implies Non-provability of Contradiction):**

Assume that a system `��` is consistent. By definition, a consistent system is one in which not every statement is provable. Specifically, this means that there is no statement `φ` such that both `φ` and `¬φ` are theorems of `��`. In particular, this applies to the contradiction symbol `⊥`, which is equivalent to a statement that is always false. If `��` were to prove `⊥`, then it would trivially prove every statement, including `⊥` itself, making `��` inconsistent. Since we have assumed `��` is consistent, it cannot prove `⊥`. Therefore, if a system is consistent, it does not prove the contradiction symbol `⊥`.

**Reverse Direction (Non-provability of Contradiction implies Consistency):**

Conversely, assume that a system `��` does not prove `⊥`. By way of contradiction, suppose that `��` is inconsistent. Then, by definition, `��` is inconsistent if and only if it proves both a statement `φ` and its negation `¬φ` for some statement `φ`. In particular, this would include the case where `��` proves `⊥`. However, this directly contradicts our assumption that `��` does not prove `⊥`. Therefore, our supposition that `��` is inconsistent leads to a contradiction, and we must conclude that `��` is consistent. Thus, if a system does not prove `⊥`, it is consistent.

Since both directions have been established, we conclude that a system `��` is consistent if and only if it does not prove the contradiction symbol `⊥`.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

informal_statement: If a logical theory is inconsistent, then it entails every possible statement (the principle of explosion).
informal_proof: Assume we have a consistent logical system where we can derive both a statement and its negation, creating an inconsistency. Let \( T \) be such an inconsistent theory. By definition, an inconsistent theory allows the derivation of any statement \( \phi \). This is a fundamental property in classical logic, known as the principle of explosion. The proof typically proceeds as follows: Given the inconsistency in \( T \), we can derive both \( \phi \) and \( \neg \phi \). Using disjunctive syllogism or other logical principles, we can construct \( \phi \) from these derivations, thereby showing that an inconsistent theory indeed entails any statement \( \phi \). This demonstrates that inconsistency undermines the ability to reason meaningfully within the system, as everything becomes provable.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by simp [Inconsistent]

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by
  simp [Inconsistent, Set.ext_iff, theory]

lemma not_inconsistent_iff_consistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ⟨h⟩, by rintro ⟨h⟩; exact h⟩

alias ⟨_, Consistent.not_inc⟩ := not_inconsistent_iff_consistent

lemma not_consistent_iff_inconsistent {𝓢 : S} :
    ¬Consistent 𝓢 ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent]

alias ⟨_, Inconsistent.not_con⟩ := not_consistent_iff_inconsistent

lemma consistent_iff_exists_unprovable {𝓢 : S} :
    Consistent 𝓢 ↔ ∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f := by
  simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_def]

alias ⟨Consistent.exists_unprovable, _⟩ := consistent_iff_exists_unprovable

lemma Consistent.of_unprovable {𝓢 : S} {f} (h : 𝓢 ⊬ f) : Consistent 𝓢 :=
  ⟨fun hp ↦ h (hp f)⟩

lemma inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ theory 𝓢 = Set.univ := by simp [inconsistent_def, theory, Set.ext_iff]

alias ⟨Inconsistent.theory_eq, _⟩ := inconsistent_iff_theory_eq_univ

lemma Inconsistent.equiv {𝓢 𝓣 : S} (h : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h' : Inconsistent 𝓣) : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 :=
  Set.ext fun f ↦ by simp [h.theory_eq, h'.theory_eq]

lemma Inconsistent.of_ge {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Inconsistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) : Inconsistent 𝓣 :=
  fun f ↦ h (h𝓢 f)

lemma Consistent.of_le {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} (h𝓢 : Consistent 𝓢) (h : 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢) : Consistent 𝓣 :=
  ⟨fun H ↦ not_consistent_iff_inconsistent.mpr (H.of_ge h) h𝓢⟩

namespace Logic

protected def Inconsistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Inconsistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma inconsistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Inconsistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Inconsistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

protected def Consistent (Λ : Logic S) : Prop :=
  Quotient.lift Consistent (fun 𝓢 𝓣 h ↦ by simp [←not_inconsistent_iff_consistent, inconsistent_iff_theory_eq, equiv_def.mp h]) Λ

@[simp] lemma consistent_mk (𝓢 : S) : Logic.Consistent (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ↔ Consistent 𝓢 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[ext] structure Translation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  toFun : F → F'
  prf {f} : 𝓢 ⊢ f → 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f

infix:40 " ↝ " => Translation

@[ext] structure Bitranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') where
  r : 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣
  l : 𝓣 ↝ 𝓢
  r_l : r.toFun ∘ l.toFun = id
  l_r : l.toFun ∘ r.toFun = id

infix:40 " ↭ " => Bitranslation

@[ext] structure FaithfulTranslation {S S' F F'} [System F S] [System F' S'] (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : S') extends 𝓢 ↝ 𝓣 where
  prfInv {f} : 𝓣 ⊢ toFun f → 𝓢 ⊢ f

informal_statement: An inconsistent logical theory is one in which any statement, including the contradiction symbolized by $\bot$, can be proven to be true. In other words, if a theory allows for the derivation of a contradiction, then that theory is considered inconsistent.
informal_proof:
To understand why an inconsistent theory allows the proof of any statement, including $\bot$, we can break it down into steps:

1. **Definition of Inconsistency**: A theory is inconsistent if it contains at least one contradiction, meaning two statements $φ$ and $\lnot φ$ can both be proven from the theory’s axioms and rules of inference.
2. **Deriving Contradictions**: Given that both $φ$ and $\lnot φ$ are in the theory, any statement can be derived using these contradictions. This is known as the principle of explosion (ex falso quodlibet), where a contradiction allows the conclusion of any proposition.
3. **Proof of Contradiction ($\bot$)**: Specifically, if a theory is inconsistent, its axioms and rules allow the derivation of a direct contradiction, such as $φ \land \lnot φ$, which is symbolized by $\bot$.
4. **Implications for Inconsistency**: Therefore, the ability to derive $\bot$ within a theory demonstrates that the theory is inconsistent, as it permits the proof of any and all statements.

In summary, an inconsistent theory is one in which the contradiction symbol $\bot$ can be formally proven, thereby establishing the theory’s inconsistency.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic
